grammar.title: Adjective predicates with 很 / 不 (no 是)
grammar.explanation: In Chinese an adjective can be the whole predicate, so you do not need a word for "is". A one-syllable-feeling adjective usually needs 很 in front of it to sound complete: 這個電影很好看 = "This movie is good." Here 很 is often just a smoothing word, not a strong "very". To make it negative, drop 很 and put 不 before the adjective: 電視不好看. To ask about it, use 怎麼樣: 這個電影怎麼樣？
grammar.contrast: 是 + Noun. Use 是 only when the predicate is a noun (他是我的同學 "He is my classmate"). If what follows describes a quality (好看、忙、便宜), use 很 or 不 and leave 是 out.
grammar.common_error: Learners translate "is" and say 這個電影是好看 or 我是很忙. Chinese adjectives already act as verbs, so 是 must be dropped: 這個電影很好看 / 我很忙.

examples.hanzi: 我今天不忙，想在家看電視。

grammar.title: 想 + Verb: feel like / want to do
grammar.explanation: 想 before a verb means "want to / feel like" doing something. Negate it with 不想. It is softer than a demand — it is about what you'd like: 我想看電影 "I'd like to see a movie."
grammar.contrast: 想 + Noun means "to miss / think of" (我想我媽媽), while 想 + Verb means "want to do". What follows 想 decides the meaning.
grammar.common_error: Putting 不 in the wrong place, e.g. 我想不去 instead of 我不想去. 不 always goes directly in front of 想.

passage.title: 週末不看電視
passage.hanzi: 週末的時候，我不想在家看電視，我覺得電視都不好看。我和同學小明搭捷運去台北，我們想看一個新的電影。電影票很便宜，電影很好看，我們都很喜歡。後來我們去吃麵，買了一杯珍珠奶茶。小明說：「下個週末再去看電影，怎麼樣？」我說：「好！」
passage.gloss: On weekends I don't feel like staying home watching TV — I think what's on TV is all pretty bad. My classmate Xiao Ming and I took the MRT to Taipei, because we wanted to see a new movie. The tickets were cheap and the movie was great; we both really liked it. Afterwards we went for noodles and bought a bubble milk tea. Xiao Ming said, "How about we go see a movie again next weekend?" I said, "Sure!"

grammar.title: 沒 for "didn't" and "there isn't"
grammar.pattern: 主語 + 沒(有) + 動詞 / 名詞
grammar.explanation: 沒 (or 沒有) says that something did not happen or does not exist. Use 沒 + verb to say an action did not happen: 我沒喝茶 (I didn't drink tea). Use 沒有 + noun to say something is not there: 杯子裡沒有水 (There's no water in the cup). 沒 is the only way to negate 有 — you can never say 不有.
grammar.contrast: 沒 vs 不: 不 negates what you generally do, don't want, or won't do (我不喝咖啡 = I don't drink coffee); 沒 negates what did not happen in the past (我今天沒喝咖啡 = I didn't drink coffee today). Ask yourself: is this a habit/wish (不) or a past fact (沒)?
grammar.common_error: Learners add 了 after a 沒 verb, saying 我沒吃了. Since 沒 already tells you the action did not happen, drop 了: 我沒吃. The other frequent mistake is 不有 instead of 沒有.

examples.hanzi: 他沒買水果，只買了白飯。
examples.pinyin: Tā méi mǎi shuǐguǒ, zhǐ mǎi le báifàn.
examples.gloss: He didn't buy fruit, he only bought rice.
There aren't any cups on the table.

grammar.title: 先……再…… (first… then…)
grammar.pattern: 先 + 動作一 + 再 + 動作二
grammar.explanation: 先 marks the first action and 再 the next one, showing the order you do things: 先喝水，再吃飯 (drink water first, then eat).
grammar.contrast: 先……再…… vs 先……就……: 再 gives a planned order of two actions by the same person; 就 suggests one thing happens right away as a result. For everyday "first A, then B", use 再.
grammar.common_error: Learners put 再 before the first verb or leave it out entirely (先喝水，吃飯). Both 先 and 再 need to sit right before their own verbs.

examples.hanzi: 你先喝一點水，再吃白飯。
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiān hē yìdiǎn shuǐ, zài chī báifàn.

passage.title: 在家吃飯
passage.hanzi: 週末晚上，我們一家都在家吃飯。媽媽做了很多菜，桌上有白飯，也有水果。爸爸今天沒喝茶，他喝了一大杯冰水。我的杯子裡沒有水，媽媽說：「你先喝水，再吃飯。」我很喜歡在家吃飯，飯菜好吃，家裡也很舒服。
passage.gloss: On weekend evenings our whole family eats at home. Mom cooked a lot of dishes; there was rice on the table, and fruit too. Dad didn't drink tea today — he drank a big glass of ice water. There was no water in my cup, and Mom said, "Drink some water first, then eat." I really like eating at home: the food is good, and home is comfortable.
